--- title: "[OrderedCategorical]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Ordered categorical (proportional odds / cumulative logit) family. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L15-L520){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python OrderedCategorical(n_categories) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `OrderedCategorical` models an ordinal response — one with a small number of categories that have a natural order but no meaningful numeric spacing, such as a Likert scale ("disagree" / "neutral" / "agree") or a severity grade — using the proportional-odds cumulative logit model. A single set of `K - 1` ordered cutpoints (thresholds) `alpha_1 < alpha_2 < ... < alpha_{K-1}` is estimated jointly with the smooth/linear predictor `eta`, and each cutpoint defines a binary split between "category `k` or below" versus "above category `k`". Because the same `eta` (and hence the same covariate effects) is shared across all thresholds, covariate effects are assumed to shift the log-odds of being in a higher category by the same amount at every threshold — the proportional-odds assumption. Use this family for ordinal outcomes with three or more ordered levels; for a two-level (binary) response, use `Binomial` instead, and for unordered categorical responses, use `Multinomial`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_categories]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of ordered response categories `K` (must be `>= 2`). Responses passed to `GAM.fit()` should be integer-coded `1, 2, ..., K`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The response, without an intercept in the design matrix (since the cutpoints absorb it), is modeled through cumulative probabilities: $$ P(Y \le k \mid \eta) = \operatorname{expit}(\alpha_k - \eta), \qquad k = 1, \dots, K-1, $$ which is equivalent to a logit link on each cumulative probability, $g(P(Y \le k)) = \alpha_k - \eta$. Category probabilities follow by differencing: $$ P(Y = 1) = \operatorname{expit}(\alpha_1 - \eta), \qquad P(Y = K) = 1 - \operatorname{expit}(\alpha_{K-1} - \eta), $$ and for interior categories $1 < k < K$, $$ P(Y = k) = \operatorname{expit}(\alpha_k - \eta) - \operatorname{expit}(\alpha_{k-1} - \eta). $$ Because this loss does not fit the standard GLM deviance framework, `link` and `link_inverse` are the identity on `eta`, and fitting instead uses a custom `irls_update` together with an inner maximum-likelihood step (`_update_cutpoints`) that re-estimates the cutpoints `alpha` at each P-IRLS iteration. The deviance reported is $-2$ times the multinomial log-likelihood of the observed categories under the fitted probabilities. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAM to a four-level ordinal response with a smooth covariate effect: ::: {#af918931 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk from scipy.special import expit rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(-3, 3, n) eta = np.sin(x) cutpoints = np.array([-1.5, 0.0, 1.5]) y = np.empty(n) for i in range(n): probs = np.diff( np.concatenate([[0.0], expit(cutpoints - eta[i]), [1.0]]) ) y[i] = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 4], p=probs) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.OrderedCategorical(n_categories=4)) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: OrderedCategorical(K=4) Inference: REML Observations: 300 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err z value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.0143 0.0887 0.161 0.8722 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 5.02 6 51.396 2.466e-09 Total EDF: 6.02 Scale est: 1.000000 Deviance: 785.2424 Null dev: 1365.4480 Dev. expl: 42.5% GCV score: 2.725803 AIC: 797.29 BIC: 819.59 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
cutpoints Fitted cutpoints (thresholds) `alpha_1 < alpha_2 < ... < alpha_{K-1}`.
n_categories Number of ordered response categories `K`.
scale_known Whether the dispersion (scale) parameter is fixed rather than estimated.
### [cutpoints]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Fitted cutpoints (thresholds) `alpha_1 < alpha_2 < ... < alpha_{K-1}`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [cutpoints]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each cutpoint `alpha_k` defines the boundary of the cumulative logit $P(Y \le k \mid \eta) = \operatorname{expit}(\alpha_k - \eta)$ separating category `k` or below from categories above `k`. The cutpoints are estimated jointly with `eta` and are updated at every P-IRLS iteration by `_update_cutpoints`. ::: ### [n_categories]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Number of ordered response categories `K`. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [n_categories]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the value supplied to the constructor and equals `1 +` the number of cutpoints (thresholds) fitted by the model. ::: ### [scale_known]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the dispersion (scale) parameter is fixed rather than estimated. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [scale_known]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Overrides the base `Family.scale_known` (which returns `False`) because the multinomial log-likelihood underlying the proportional-odds model has no free dispersion parameter — the scale is always `1` and is never estimated during fitting. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
deviance() Total deviance, $-2$ times the multinomial log-likelihood of the observed categories.
initialize() Initialize cutpoints and the starting linear predictor before P-IRLS.
irls_update() Working response and weights for the cumulative-logit log-likelihood.
link() Identity link, `g(mu) = mu`.
link_derivative() Derivative of the identity link, `g'(mu) = 1`.
link_inverse() Identity inverse link, `g^{-1}(eta) = eta`.
log_likelihood() Log-likelihood of the observed categories, `-0.5 * deviance(y, mu)`.
simulate() Simulate ordinal category labels from the fitted cumulative-logit model.
unit_deviance() Per-observation deviance contributions, overriding the base `(y - mu)^2` default.
variance() Placeholder variance function, `V(mu) = 1`.
### [deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total deviance, $-2$ times the multinomial log-likelihood of the observed categories. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L340-L380){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python deviance(y, mu, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of the abstract `Family.deviance`. Because the proportional-odds model has a saturated log-likelihood of `0` (each observation can be assigned probability `1` to its own category), the deviance reduces to $$ D(y, \eta) = -2 \sum_i \log P(Y_i = y_i \mid \eta_i), $$ with the cumulative category probabilities $P(Y_i = k \mid \eta_i)$ computed by `_category_probs` from the current cutpoints. The `weights` argument is accepted for interface compatibility but is not applied. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed category labels, coded `1, ..., K`, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values `eta` (see `link`), shape `(n,)`. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Unused. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total deviance, or `len(y)` as a placeholder if the model has not yet been fitted (cutpoints not initialized). ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Initialize cutpoints and the starting linear predictor before P-IRLS. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L498-L517){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Overrides the base `Family.initialize` (which returns `y` unchanged). Sets the initial cutpoints via `_init_cutpoints`, which derives each threshold `alpha_k` from the empirical logit of `P(Y <= k + 1)`, and starts the linear predictor `eta` at zero for every observation (i.e. an intercept-only model at the first iteration). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed category labels, coded `1, ..., K`, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting linear predictor values, an array of zeros with shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [irls_update()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Working response and weights for the cumulative-logit log-likelihood. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L264-L338){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python irls_update(y, mu, eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific override of the base `Family.irls_update` (whose default returns `None` and falls back to the standard GLM formula). On the first call the cutpoints are initialized via `_init_cutpoints`; on every call the cutpoints are then re-estimated by maximum likelihood via `_update_cutpoints` given the current `eta`, implementing the two-block (cutpoints, then smooth) coordinate ascent that fits the proportional-odds model. Category probabilities are computed by `_category_probs`, and for each observation `i` in its observed category `k = y_int[i] - 1` the first and second derivatives of the log-likelihood $$ \ell_i(\eta_i) = \log\bigl[P(Y_i = k+1 \mid \eta_i)\bigr] $$ with respect to `eta_i` are computed in closed form (differing at the boundary categories `k = 0` and `k = K - 1` versus interior categories). The working weight is the (clipped, non-negative) negative second derivative, and the working response is the Newton step $z_i = \eta_i + (d\ell_i/d\eta_i) / W_i$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed category labels, coded `1, ..., K`, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Unused; `OrderedCategorical` uses `eta` directly (see `link`). [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current linear predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple of NDArray, NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(z, W)`, the working response and working weights, each shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Identity link, `g(mu) = mu`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L184-L203){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `OrderedCategorical` does not use a conventional mean-to-linear-predictor link: the object passed around as `mu` throughout P-IRLS is already the linear predictor `eta`, and the actual cumulative-logit transformation is applied internally by `_category_probs` and `irls_update`. This method and `link_inverse` are therefore the identity, present only to satisfy the `Family` interface. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values to pass through unchanged, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `mu`, unchanged. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the identity link, `g'(mu) = 1`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L224-L242){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Since `link` is the identity, its derivative is constant. This method is unused in practice because `OrderedCategorical` overrides `irls_update` to compute the working response and weights directly from the cumulative-logit log-likelihood, bypassing the standard GLM `link`/`variance` formula. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values used only to determine the output shape, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Identity inverse link, `g^{-1}(eta) = eta`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L205-L222){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Mirrors `link`: since `OrderedCategorical` treats `mu` and `eta` as the same quantity and derives category probabilities directly from `eta` via `_category_probs`, no transformation is needed here. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values to pass through unchanged, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `eta`, unchanged. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Log-likelihood of the observed categories, `-0.5 * deviance(y, mu)`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L418-L444){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, mu, scale, *, weights=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of the abstract `Family.log_likelihood`. Since `deviance` is already defined as `-2` times the multinomial log-likelihood, this simply inverts that relationship; the `scale` parameter is ignored because `OrderedCategorical` has no free dispersion parameter (see `scale_known`). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed category labels, coded `1, ..., K`, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values `eta` (see `link`), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Unused; the scale is fixed at `1` for this family. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional prior weights, forwarded to `deviance`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total multinomial log-likelihood. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate ordinal category labels from the fitted cumulative-logit model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L461-L496){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(mu, scale, rng) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of the abstract `Family.simulate`. For each observation, category probabilities are computed from the current cutpoints and `eta` via `_category_probs`, and a category in `1, ..., K` is drawn from the resulting categorical distribution using `rng.choice`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values `eta` (see `link`), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Unused; this family has no free dispersion parameter (see `scale_known`). [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [np.random.Generator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `numpy.random.Generator` instance used to draw the simulated categories. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated category labels, coded `1, ..., K`, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Notes {.doc-notes} Raises `RuntimeError` if called before the model has been fitted (i.e. before `initialize` has set `cutpoints`). ### [unit_deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Per-observation deviance contributions, overriding the base `(y - mu)^2` default. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L382-L416){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python unit_deviance(y, mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific per-observation deviance so that the total returned by `deviance` decomposes as `sum(unit_deviance(y, mu))`. For observation `i` in category `y_i`, the contribution is $$ d_i = -2 \log P(Y_i = y_i \mid \eta_i), $$ using the cumulative category probabilities from `_category_probs`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed category labels, coded `1, ..., K`, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values `eta` (see `link`), shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Per-observation deviance contributions $d_i$, shape `(n,)`, or an array of ones if the model has not yet been fitted (cutpoints not initialized). ::: ### [variance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Placeholder variance function, `V(mu) = 1`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/families/ordered_categorical.py#L244-L262){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python variance(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `OrderedCategorical` does not fit the standard GLM variance-function framework: its working weights are instead derived from the second derivative of the multinomial log-likelihood with respect to `eta` inside `irls_update`. This method returns a constant and is not used by the fitting loop. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Values used only to determine the output shape, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones, shape `(n,)`. :::
